**Direction: In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.**

To mind one's P's and Q's

options.text: To be polite and careful in one's behaviour and speech
To make amends after a fight

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"To be polite and careful in one's behaviour and speech."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"To mind one's P's and Q's"** means to be cautious and attentive to one's words and actions. (अपने शब्दों और कार्यों के प्रति सतर्क और चौकस रहना)

 
 
• **Example**: *I have **to mind my p's and q's**__ when I'm with my grandmother.*
 
 
 
• The phrase originated from the printing industry, where typesetters had to be careful not to confuse the letters** "p"** and **"q" **as they looked very similar.
 
• The correct answer is Option 1.

Photosynthesis can be **__hindered__** by extreme temperatures.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"discouraged."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**hindered**" means to make it more difficult for somebody/something to do something. (व्‍यक्ति या वस्‍तु के लिए कठिनाई पैदा करना, किसी के काम में बाधा डालना)

 
 
• **Example**: A lot of scientific work is **hindered **by lack of money.
 
 
 
• The synonym for **hindered **is **discouraged**.
 
• "**Discouraged**" means to stop somebody doing something, especially by making him/her realize that it would not be successful or a good idea. ((किसी व्‍यक्ति को) निरुत्‍साहित करना (यह समझाते हुए कि सफलता नहीं मिलेगी))
 
 
• **Example**: I **discouraged **Jai from giving up his job.
 
 
 
• The sentence means that extreme temperatures can negatively impact photosynthesis. 
 
• The correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Option 1, **gained**, means to acquire or obtain and is not a synonym for hindered. (वस्‍तु तक पहुँचना या प्राप्‍त करना, विशेषतः अपेक्षित या अभीष्‍ट वस्‍तु; पाना)
 
• Option 2, **revert**, means to return to a previous state or condition and is not a synonym for hindered. (पूर्व दशा या क्रिया में लौट जाना)
 
• Option 3, **tolerated**, means to endure or allow and is not a synonym for hindered. (सहन या बरदाश्‍त करना (किसी अरुचिकर या अस्‍वीकार्य वस्‍तु को), नापसंद स्थितियों को भी बने रहने देना या उनके साथ रहना)

questions.question:
**Direction: A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.**

Nigeria ______restrictions in place since 2015 in a bid to boost local production.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"has had."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in the present perfect tense, which uses the auxiliary verb **"has/have"** and the past participle (V3) form of the main verb.
 
• **Structure: Subject + has/have + V3 + Object**
 
 
• **Example: ***She **has done**__ her work.*
 
 
 
• **"Nigeria"** is a singular subject, so it needs the singular form of the verb **"has".**
 
• The phrase **"in place since 2015"** indicates a duration of time that started in the past and continues to the present.
 
• The correct answer is Option 1.

 

**Correct sentence**:* **Nigeria __**has had**__ restrictions in place since 2015 in a bid to boost local production. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Option 2, **"have had",** is grammatically incorrect because it uses a plural verb form with a singular subject.
 
• Option 3,** "have has",** is also incorrect because it uses two auxiliary verbs together.
 
• Option 4,** "had has"**, is incorrect because it uses the past simple form of "have" instead of the present perfect form.
